edges.description: Oxidized LDL infiltrates the arterial intima, recruiting monocytes and triggering foam cell formation (atherogenesis initiation)
Inflammatory plaque destabilization thins fibrous caps and promotes thrombosis, driving acute cardiovascular events
Chronic hyperglycemia generates advanced glycation end products (AGEs), accelerating micro- and macrovascular complications
Elevated blood pressure increases cardiac workload and accelerates atherosclerotic plaque progression
Atorvastatin inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, reducing hepatic LDL synthesis
Metformin improves hepatic insulin sensitivity and reduces gluconeogenesis
Ramipril and amlodipine reduce systemic vascular resistance
Familial hypercholesterolemia variants (LDLR, APOB, PCSK9 gain-of-function) elevate baseline LDL cholesterol
9p21.3 risk locus and APOE4 confer lipid-independent cardiovascular risk through endothelial dysfunction and platelet hyperreactivity
Chronic HPA axis activation elevates cortisol, driving hepatic gluconeogenesis and peripheral insulin resistance
Sustained sympathetic overdrive and systemic inflammation from chronic stress independently increase cardiovascular event risk

messages.content: You are a clinical epidemiologist specializing in cardiometabolic causal inference...
Research question: What factors drive this patient's cardiovascular risk, given 3 years of Doctolib medical records including prescriptions, lab results, and vital signs?

I'll construct a latent causal model for this patient's cardiovascular risk trajectory. I'm including two unobserved confounders that are clinically important but not captured in routine Doctolib records: genetic predisposition and psychosocial stress.
messages.reasoning: Patient has T2DM, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia. Key observed constructs: lipid burden (statin-modifiable), vascular inflammation (mediator of lipid→CV pathway), glycemic control (metformin-modifiable), arterial pressure (ACE-i + CCB modifiable). Medication adherence is exogenous. Two critical unobserved confounders: (1) genetic predisposition — LDLR/APOE variants affect both lipid levels and CV risk independently, creating confounding on the lipid→CV pathway that may be resolvable via frontdoor through inflammation; (2) psychosocial stress — cortisol/HPA axis affects both glycemic control and CV risk, creating confounding that has no mediator to exploit.

messages.content: The latent model captures 8 constructs (6 observed, 2 unobserved) and 11 directed edges. The contemporaneous subgraph is acyclic. Notably, lipid_burden affects cardiovascular_risk only through vascular_inflammation (no direct edge), enabling potential frontdoor identification despite genetic confounding.
